walkthroughs.body_html:
Unit A2 2: Composing — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Unit A2 2: Composing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Unit A2 2: Composing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Repeating a melodic idea immediately at a higher or lower pitch is called what?
options: Inversion
Sequence
Retrograde
Pedal

mcqs.q: Writing parts that suit the range and technique of each instrument is described as what?
options: Idiomatic writing
Strophic writing
Aleatoric writing
Heterophonic writing

mcqs.q: A texture of one melody supported by chordal accompaniment is called what?
options: Monophonic
Homophonic
Polyphonic
Antiphonal

mcqs.q: Augmentation develops a theme by doing what?
options: Playing it backwards
Lengthening its note values proportionally
Raising it an octave
Removing its rests

mcqs.q: Does repeating an idea over and over count as developing it?
options: Development just means repeating your main idea many times.
Inversion means doubling the melody in octaves.
Development means deleting the idea and writing a new one each phrase.
No - development means transforming the idea, for example by sequence, inversion, augmentation or fragmentation.

mcqs.q: Will using as many instruments as possible make a composition better?
options: No - effective composing controls texture, using contrast between thick and thin scoring; every part should earn its place.
A bigger ensemble automatically means a more impressive composition.
Compositions are only allowed to use four instruments.
Development means deleting the idea and writing a new one each phrase.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between inversion and retrograde?
options: Compositions are only allowed to use four instruments.
Inversion turns the melodic intervals upside down; retrograde plays the idea backwards in time.
Inversion means doubling the melody in octaves.
Inversion means playing the melody backwards.

sequence.term: Choose the brief or free idea
sequence.def: Composing starts by fixing what the piece must do
Jot riffs, motifs and progressions before developing anything
Grow the strongest material into full musical sections
Decide the overall form once the sections exist
Notate and record the finished piece
Last of all: submit score/recording plus the required log
